title: Tabbouleh
subtitle: Herby bulgur wheat salad with tomato and lemon
excerpt: A Levantine salad where flat-leaf parsley is the main ingredient and bulgur wheat plays a supporting role. Very finely chopped parsley, mint, tomato and cucumber are dressed with olive oil and plenty of lemon juice. The proportions here follow the traditional Lebanese approach rather than the Western version, where grain tends to dominate.
sourceNotes: Tabbouleh is one of the defining dishes of Levantine cuisine, originating in the mountains of Lebanon and Syria; it is traditionally herb-dominant with the bulgur playing a supporting role, unlike many Western interpretations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the bulgur and chop the herbs ahead, but dress the salad no more than 30 minutes before serving or the herbs will wilt.

content.text: The parsley must be chopped very finely, almost to a powder in places. Take your time with this; a rough chop gives the salad a coarser texture and a stronger raw flavour. Use a large sharp knife and rock it back and forth over the herbs, gathering them in and chopping again until very fine. Remove the tomato seeds before dicing; they release water that dilutes the dressing.

Place the bulgur wheat in a heatproof bowl. Pour over enough boiling water to cover by 2cm (about 250ml). Cover with a plate and leave to soak for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. If any water remains, drain through a fine sieve. Spread on a tray to cool and dry slightly.

While the bulgur soaks, finely chop the parsley and mint. Take your time; the finer the herbs, the better the texture of the finished salad. Dice the tomatoes (seeds removed) and cucumber into 5mm pieces. Finely slice the spring onions.
Combine the cooled bulgur, herbs, tomatoes, cucumber and spring onions in a large bowl. Dress with the lemon juice and olive oil. Toss well and season generously with salt.
Taste and adjust lemon and salt. The salad should taste very fresh and sharp. Serve within 30 minutes of dressing; after that the herbs begin to wilt and lose their vibrancy.

items.symptom: Salad is watery at the bottom of the bowl
items.cause: Tomato seeds were not removed, or bulgur was not fully drained
items.fix: Drain off the liquid, taste and re-dress with a little extra olive oil to compensate for any diluted lemon. Next time remove tomato seeds and spread the bulgur to cool on a tray after soaking.

items.cause: Under-seasoned or not enough lemon juice
items.fix: Tabbouleh needs significantly more salt and lemon than you might expect. Add both in small increments and taste after each addition.
